items.title: Damage assessment, repairs underway after Seberang Jaya Hospital ceiling leaks
items.summary: The Penang Health Department said the hospital's engineering unit and building management concessionaire were conducting a comprehensive assessment and taking steps to contain the damage. "Hospital personnel took prompt and appropriate action to manage affected patients and safeguard medical equipment at the relevant locations," it said in a Facebook statement. The leaks followed an unusually heavy thunderstorm accompanied by strong winds between 5.45pm and 7pm, which caused rainwater to overflow at several locations in Block A (the old block) and Block B (the new block).

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysia considers accelerating quantum migration to boost data security
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia is considering accelerating its quantum migration process to strengthen national data security amid advances in quantum computing technology that are expected to pose new challenges to cybersecurity systems. He said the collaboration would involve establishing a research and development space to facilitate faster and more secure quantum migration in Malaysia. He said the emergence of quantum computers on the market was expected to pose significant challenges to existing cryptography and encryption methods used to safeguard data.

items.title: Deepavali traffic remains smooth nationwide, but return rush expected later today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Traffic flow on most major expressways nationwide remained smooth as of 8am today, but vehicle numbers are expected to increase later in the day as motorists return from the Deepavali and additional school holidays. However, a Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) spokesperson said congestion was reported along the southbound stretch of the North-South Expressway (PLUS), from Yong Peng towards Ayer Hitam, following an accident. The spokesperson said CCTV monitoring had yet to show a significant increase in traffic heading towards the Klang Valley, possibly due to the additional holiday today.

items.title: Flood victim numbers rise in Perak, fall in Selangor
items.summary: The situation in Hilir Perak saw the number of victims increase to 439 people from 130 families this morning, compared with 414 people from 123 families yesterday evening. Meanwhile, 26 victims from seven families remained at the Manjung Community Hall PPS, comprising residents of Pekan Beruas, Taman Beruas, Taman Desa, Perumahan Awam, Taman Seri Delima, Taman Limau Emas, Taman Anggerik, Kampung Kilang, Kampung Dendang and Kampung Paya Lima. In Selangor, the situation improved, with the number of victims at PPS decreasing to 215 people from 55 families as of 8am today, compared with 507 people from 143 families yesterday.

items.title: Melaka election 2026: What the parties are promising, where the battles are and what could decide the vote
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — As campaigning for the 16th Melaka state election enters its second week, rival parties are seeking to win over voters with promises of economic growth, political stability and reform, while new alliances face the test of whether their supporters will vote across party lines. Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) are banking on their joint electoral machinery, Pakatan Harapan (PH) is challenging the incumbent administration’s record, and smaller parties are seeking to distinguish themselves through reform pledges and alternative campaign strategies. PH is contesting 24 seats, followed by BN with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) with 16, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with seven, PN with five and Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (Putra) with one.

items.title: Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Sabah under rain alert until Wednesday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy and persistent rain is expected in parts of Kelantan and Terengganu until Wednesday, with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issuing a severe continuous rain warning. In Kelantan, the warning covers Bachok, Kota Baru, Tumpat, Pasir Mas and Pasir Puteh, while in Terengganu it affects Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus. The affected areas in Kelantan are Tanah Merah, Machang, Kuala Krai and Jeli, while in Terengganu the alert covers Hulu Terengganu.

items.title: Johari: Reliance on foreign workers must be reduced
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Malaysia must reduce its dependence on foreign labour in phases by expanding the adoption of automation, robotics and digital technology, particularly within the manufacturing sector. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said this approach is crucial to ensure the sustainability of domestic industry without remaining perpetually reliant on foreign workers to meet operational needs. Johari said foreign labour is still required for roles categorised as 3D — dirty, difficult and dangerous — but industry must transition towards a more sustainable business model.

items.title: MITI to consult Customs, MOF over machinery import duty issue
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The issue of machinery import duties allegedly being imposed on local companies despite them securing exemption approvals from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) will be raised with the Customs Department and the Finance Ministry (MoF). Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the matter was raised by several industry operators during a dialogue session with the business community in Melaka yesterday. He said some companies claimed they were forced to pay duties upon despite already possessing exemption approval letters from Mida.

items.title: Remembering 2014’s great flood, Kelantan firefighters prepare for another big test
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 9 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM) is drawing on its experience in handling the massive 2014 floods to strengthen its preparedness for potential extreme disasters in the state, said its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan. He said the extraordinary scale of the 2014 floods, which affected vast areas of the state, posed significant challenges to rescue operations. He said such situations underscored the importance of assistance from other states, particularly in terms of personnel and assets, to ensure rescue operations could continue when disasters exceeded the capacity of state agencies.

items.title: Merz picks Ilse Aigner to become Germany's first woman president
items.summary: BERLIN: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Sunday he intended to appoint Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner as the country's next president, in 2027, making her the first woman in the post. He made his announcement at a dinner for leaders of his centre-right CDU party, confirming information leaked last week by party sources. Aigner, 61, belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the CDU.

items.title: How a digital bank's collapse toppled Paraguay's president
items.summary: FOR years, Paraguay's digital bank, Ueno, stood out as a homegrown success story, luring roughly half the country's people to open accounts and offering many the opportunity to hold a bank account for the very first time. But over just five days this week, the bank collapsed, freezing the savings of nearly three million customers — in a country of 6.5 million people — and triggering the country's deepest political crisis in more than a decade. Authorities quickly arrested Pena, an economist and close ally of US President Donald Trump, and prosecutors charged him on Saturday with breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

items.title: Mexico arrests another major Jalisco Cartel kingpin
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: Mexican authorities announced on Sunday the arrest of a regional leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), one of the country's two main criminal groups. The arrested suspect is Rafael Alvarez, alias "R2," who headed a cell linked to homicides, drug trafficking and extortion of avocado industry entrepreneurs. The drug gang operates in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan.

items.title: From scandalous game to mass entertainment: is GTA going soft?
items.summary: But with days to go before the release of the hugely popular video game's new instalment, players and analysts are wondering if changes in studio Rockstar's creative team suggest a possible shift into less controversial territory, and an end to the punk-rock transgressions that helped turn GTA into a cultural phenomenon. "It's a valid question," said expert Olivier Mauco, author of the book "GTA IV, the Dark Side of the American Dream", noting the various presentations of the new game had so far put the franchise's famed political incorrectness "much less front and centre." For expert Christopher Dring, GTA's "punk rock" style is part of Rockstar's DNA.

items.title: Trump: Offer of White House press secretary role to Dana White was a joke
items.summary: WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump said Sunday that he was only joking when he offered the role of White House press secretary to Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White earlier in the weekend. "I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump told reporters on the tarmac of his namesake airport in Florida. The press secretary role – traditionally the most visible administration role after the president – has been vacant since Katie Zacharia stepped down on October 16 after less than a week on the job.--AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Penang police clarify abuse victim’s custody timeline after protection concerns raised
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 9 — Penang police said an 11-year-old girl allegedly sexually abused by her father was placed in her paternal grandmother’s temporary care on Oct 16, the day he was arrested and remanded, and handed to her mother on Oct 21, three days before his remand ended. Penang Chief Police Officer Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the girl’s school principal lodged a report with the Criminal Investigation Division of the Southwest District Police Headquarters at 11.15 am on Oct 16, and the suspect was arrested at about 5.30 pm that day and remanded until Oct 24. “The girl was referred to the One Stop Crisis Centre (OSCC) at Penang Hospital on Oct 17 and remained in the paediatric ward until Oct 21, when the Southwest District Social Welfare Department (JKM) handed her to her biological mother,” he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: Police raid home of ex-president of Paraguay
items.summary: Authorities last week intervened to seize Ueno Bank, a popular online lender that held accounts for nearly half of Paraguay's 6.5 million people, plus more than US$800 million in government funds. Pena, who came to power in 2023, owned shares in the bank's holding company, Ueno Holding, until he sold them last year. They say Ueno Bank received deposits from government entities even as it granted questionable loans to companies linked to Ueno executives.

items.title: Fahmi says child safety and cybersecurity must keep pace with AI
items.summary: He said innovation must be accompanied by appropriate safeguards to protect users and build public confidence in digital technologies. He said the declaration reflected three priorities central to Malaysia’s national digital agenda, which were ensuring meaningful connectivity, promoting digital inclusion and fostering a safe and trusted digital environment. Fahmi said digital transformation must create opportunities for everyone regardless of geographical location or level of digital readiness.

items.title: Kelantan braces for floods as nine districts face days of relentless rain
items.summary: “In Kota Bharu, areas at risk are located within the Kelantan River Basin, while in Tumpat, they are within the Golok River Basin, covering Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua and Sungai Kelaboran,” it said in a statement tonight. In Bachok, areas at risk are within the Kemasin River Basin, including Sungai Jelawat, Sungai Kemasin, Saliran PKS, Saliran KADA drainage and Sungai Bator. The Semerak River Basin, covering Sungai Lubuk Nibong, Sungai Melor, Sungai Gunong and Sungai Semerak, is also at risk of flooding.

items.title: Teenage girl dies in fall from ninth floor of parking lot
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A 17-year-old girl was found dead early yesterday at the Selasih 1Malaysia Civil Servants Housing Project (PPA1M) in Presint 17. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the victim was found unconscious about 5.45am. He said the teen was pronounced dead at the scene.

items.title: 11 cars, 23 motorcycles destroyed in fire at workshop
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Eleven cars and 23 motorcycles were destroyed when a workshop in Kampung Jerang Belangga, Kota Sarang Semut, caught fire early today. The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department said firemen from the Guar Cempedeka, Pendang and Jalan Raja stations arrived at the scene about 20 minutes after a distress call was received. "The fire was brought under control at 3.53am.

items.title: Pakatan steps up social media push to win Melaka’s young and first-time voters
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is stepping up efforts to win over young voters, particularly first-time voters, through more targeted campaigning, including the use of social media and face-to-face engagement, in the 16th Melaka state election. Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said campaign strategies must adapt to changing communication trends, particularly when reaching out to young people who are more active on social media. “While social media is an important campaign platform, traditional methods of engaging directly with voters must not be overlooked.

items.title: 24 families lose everything in fire at Kanowit longhouse
items.summary: A Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said the fire was reported at 1.39am, adding that firemen arrived at the scene at 2.30am. The firemen, he said, were from the Kanowit and Sibu Jaya stations. The operation involved 16 firemen in two Light Fire Rescue Tenders and a pickup truck.

items.title: Brunei’s record 102kg syabu bust snares Malaysian suspect with two prior records
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — A Malaysian man arrested by Brunei authorities with more than 100 kilogrammes (kg) of suspected syabu at the Sungai Tujoh Control Post along the Brunei-Miri border on Oct 31 has two previous criminal records. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 46-year-old suspect from Miri was believed to be on his way to Sabah when he was detained. He said the department received information from Brunei’s Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) regarding the arrest of the man, along with about 100kg of suspected syabu valued at an estimated RM5 million.

items.title: Four boat skippers, 30 undocumented migrants nabbed at illegal jetty in Nibong
items.summary: District police chief Superintendent Mohd Haki Hasbullah said the raid kicked off at 9.45am based on police intelligence. "Checks at the location led police to the arrests of 34 people, including 30 undocumented migrants comprising 18 men and 12 women from Myanmar. Haki said police also found a bottle containing what is believed to be 450ml of ketum juice in a Perodua Myvi parked nearby.

items.title: Malaysian embassy monitoring situation in Krakow after shooting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian embassy in Warsaw is closely monitoring the situation in Krakow following a shooting incident at the Main Market Square on Saturday. "Malaysians in Poland are also encouraged to register their details with the embassy," the embassy said in a Facebook post last night. They may also contact the embassy via email at mwwarsaw@kln.gov.my.

items.title: Watch the rivers: Flood threat looms over Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin
items.summary: “Also involved are the Sungai Cherating Basin (Sungai Cherating), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Lepar), and Sungai Penor Basin (Sungai Penor),” said the statement. For the Pekan district, the areas involved are the Sungai Bebar Basin (Sungai Bebar), Sungai Miang Basin (Sungai Miang), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Pahang, Sungai Pahang Tua and Sungai Mentiga), while the Sungai Mercung Basin (Sungai Mercung) is also included. In addition, in Rompin, it will involve areas in the Sungai Endau Basin (Sungai Endau and Sungai Anak Endau), Sungai Rompin Basin (Sungai Rompin, Sungai Pukin, Sungai Kepasing, Sungai Keratong, Sungai Jeram, Sungai Gayong, Sungai Chanis, Sungai Buan) as well as the Sungai Pontian Pahang Basin (Sungai Pontian Pahang).

items.title: Monkeys on road leave two Terengganu police officers injured in patrol crash
items.summary: HULU TERENGGANU, Nov 9 — Two police officers were injured after the patrol car they were in skidded and overturned while trying to avoid a group of monkeys at Kilometre 4, Jalan Simpang Bukit Kepah-Tapah, near Kampung Kepah, here yesterday. Hulu Terengganu district police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said that in the incident at about 4.30pm, Lance Corporal Muhammad Amirul Hafiz Ahmad, 26, and Corporal Khairil Azlan Abdul Latif, 44, from the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Hulu Terengganu district police headquarters were carrying out traffic enforcement patrol duties in the Hulu Terengganu area. Sharudin said Muhammad Amirul Hafiz, who fractured his left arm, and his colleague Khairil Azlan, who experienced pain in his jaw, were sent to Hulu Terengganu Hospital for treatment.

items.title: Following Kraków attack, Malaysian embassy urges citizens to stay connected
items.summary: The embassy said it remained in contact with the Malaysian community in Kraków to ensure their safety. “The Embassy encourages Malaysians in Poland to register their details with the Embassy,” it said in a Facebook post on Sunday. The embassy also extended its condolences to the victims, their families and the people of Poland.

items.title: A-G flags flaws in Najib's house arrest documents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Attorney-general Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar yesterday questioned the diligence exercised in preparing official judicial documents for the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest order. Commenting on the Kuala Lumpur High Court's Order of Discharge relating to the former prime minister's sentence, which has raised questions among legal practitioners, he said such issues should not have arisen had the parties involved scrutinised every detail. [[nid:1573703]] The A-GC's decision drew criticism from Istana Negara, which said any arguments disputing the conditional pardon granted to Najib could amount to defying the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree.

items.title: Freiburg third after beating Union, Leverkusen beat Cologne in derby
items.summary: BERLIN: Freiburg kept hot on the heels of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund with a comfortable 2-0 home win over lowly Union Berlin to return to third in the Bundesliga table on Sunday, while Bayer Leverkusen sunk derby rivals Cologne. Freiburg pressured Union captain Rani Khedira into an own goal nine minutes after half-time and Yuito Suzuki scored another as the hosts won despite their own skipper Vincenzo Grifo missing a penalty. Last season's beaten Europa League finalists are third on 19 points, two behind Bayern and Dortmund with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference.

items.title: Rubio: Progress made on 'security infrastructure' after Ukraine war
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Sunday that some progress has been made on what the "security infrastructure" of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia, adding that talks this week could lead to further advances. Rubio's comments, ahead of his travel to Paris for talks with G7 foreign ministers, come as Russia-Ukraine negotiations under US mediation have been set for Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi. A key issue is, he said, "What is the postwar security infrastructure of Ukraine and more broadly of the European continent going to look like?"

items.title: Timeless principles of true leadership
items.summary: LETTERS: Selangor recently marked a truly historic milestone as the state celebrated the Silver Jubilee of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah. Reflecting on this quarter-century, many people highlighted the Sultan's deep love for everyone he serves. He reminded everyone that Selangor's greatest strength is not just its business and economic success.

items.title: CAAM targets year-end framework to scale up Malaysia's low-altitude economy
items.summary: Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the framework is aims to provide a common direction for government agencies, industry players, manufacturers and operators as Malaysia scales up the use of low-altitude airspace while maintaining safety and public confidence. LAE refers to economic and public service activities conducted within low-altitude airspace using emerging aviation technologies and services. Norazman said normal civil aviation traffic generally operates above 4000 feet except around airport areas, leaving lower-altitude airspace that could be used for other applications.

items.title: Wage hike may push plantation costs up 9pct
items.summary: Industry players said the increase is expected to raise labour costs for plantation companies, which have limited ability to pass on higher expenses as crude palm oil (CPO) prices are largely determined by global market conditions. Malaysian Palm Oil Association (MPOA) chief executive Roslin Azmy Hassan said plantation companies will have to absorb most of the additional expenses, putting pressure on profit margins, particularly if CPO prices remain subdued. SD Guthrie said higher labour costs would accelerate efforts to improve productivity through mechanisation, better tools, enhanced skills and more efficient estate operations.

items.title: PNB unfazed by MSCI's Indonesia concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) has ruled out a blanket withdrawal from Indonesian investments following MSCI's proposal to reclassify the country's equity market, saying the index provider's concerns do not, by themselves, justify an exit. PNB said it has no direct holdings in Indonesian equities. MSCI's latest move, announced on Oct 15, proposes reclassifying Indonesia from an emerging market to a standalone market, citing persistent concerns over opaque shareholding structures, suspected coordinated trading and weaknesses in market governance.

items.title: Nvidia probes CEO Huang amid reports of Chinese spy links to Singapore-based firm
items.summary: NEW YORK: Chip giant Nvidia's board announced Sunday it opened a probe into Chief Executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. The executive, Alice Huang – also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang – developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said. The Times said Huang's relationship with the other Huang could have given her insights into Trump's thinking around AI.

items.title: Pope takes Milei to task over cuts affecting Argentina's poor
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES: Pope Leo XIV delivered a stinging critique of President Javier Milei's harsh austerity measures Sunday, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause. Milei famously insulted Francis for his pro-poor teachings. Leo said he was "retracing" Francis's steps.

items.title: Make Sarawak's wealth work harder
items.summary: For Sarawak, the lasting return should include competitive local suppliers and people whose skills command higher wages. An industrial facility may produce for decades. Sarawak's Post Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030 already connects economic prosperity with social inclusivity and environmental sustainability.

items.title: Mentakab's last newsdealer keeps print tradition alive [WATCH]
items.summary: TEMERLOH: As younger generations embrace digital platforms, 70-year-old K. Mutusamy is determined to keep the tradition of printed newspapers and magazines alive in Mentakab. There was a time when readers would wait outside my shop as early as 5.30am to buy newspapers, while some even made advance bookings for magazines. Dozens of newspaper agents and paperboys would gather outside the shop to sort out their copies," he told the New Straits Times .

items.title: Analysts weigh BN-PN and PH manifestos ahead of Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: The Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional joint election manifesto offers a structured development agenda for the state, although Pakatan Harapan has put forward several distinctive proposals aimed at youth entrepreneurship and inclusive economic growth, a political analyst said. Universiti Malaya senior political science lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the BN-PN manifesto stood out for its measurable economic commitments, particularly its targets of attracting RM30 billion in investments, creating 25,000 jobs and delivering 25,000 affordable homes over five years. He said the pledges directly address economic opportunities and living standards, providing clear benchmarks against which the coalition's performance could be assessed.

items.title: Melaka election: Final push to win over voters
items.summary: MELAKA: More flags bearing the logos of coalitions and parties contesting the state election have been put up in public areas over the weekend as campaigning intensifies in the final stretch. Against this backdrop, the coming week is crucial for the 79 candidates contesting the polls, as they have about five days until campaigning ends at 11.59pm on Friday to make their final pitches, reinforce their campaign messages and win the support of 687,697 voters. Political leaders and observers have differing views on whether voters have already made up their minds.

items.title: Fighting scammers with AI and data: How Budget 2027 is sharpening Malaysia’s cybercrime defences
items.summary: Budget 2027 introduces three initiatives aimed at addressing online threats: an artificial intelligence (AI) application developed by the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC), an upgrade to the police’s system for detecting child exploitation, and an expanded internet safety campaign in schools. How will these initiatives help protect Malaysians from online threats? A new AI application to check before you pay Under Budget 2027, the NSRC will develop an AI application that allows users to check suspicious phone numbers, bank accounts and links before making a transaction.

items.title: BN-Perikatan cooperation may not translate into full voter support, says Melaka Pakatan chairman
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 16th Melaka state election does not guarantee a full transfer of votes between their supporters, despite the apparent advantage of such an arrangement on paper. State Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari said supporters of the two coalitions might not necessarily embrace the cooperation, while new voters could also influence the election outcome. For example, based on the Negeri Sembilan state election results, the highest vote transfer rate recorded was 70 per cent.

items.title: Police secure remand of nine suspects over deadly Sibu brawl
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 8 — Nine suspects have been remanded for seven days until Nov 15 to assist in the investigation into the death of a 19-year-old male believed to have been stabbed during a brawl here yesterday. Sibu District Police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspects, aged between 16 and 42, were brought to court at 7.15 am today for the remand application. He said a post-mortem examination completed today revealed that the victim died of chest injuries.

items.title: Heavy rain triggers flash floods in Taman Sri Muda, no displacement reported
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — No evacuations have been carried out in Taman Sri Muda, Section 25 here following flash floods triggered by heavy rain this afternoon, which were also captured in videos circulating on social media. He said monitoring was also being carried out in other high-risk areas, including Jalan Kebun Bunga in Section 22, Section 13 and Jalan Kebun. Earlier, social media users shared updates on flash floods following heavy rain between 3 pm and 5 pm today.

items.title: Second 5G network achieves 90pc coverage ahead of schedule, says Fahmi
items.summary: He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia’s transition towards a dual 5G network model aimed at strengthening competition, encouraging investment and improving telecommunications service quality. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made significant investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) since 2020. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial progress in 5G deployment, with the second network achieving 90 per cent coverage nine months ahead of schedule.

items.title: Malaysia to leverage AI and satellite networks for disaster preparedness
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 8 — Malaysia sees significant opportunities to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience, said Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil. He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies. Fahmi said Malaysia was placing greater emphasis on strengthening emergency telecommunications capabilities to ensure essential communications remained available when conventional networks were disrupted.

items.title: Nations must decide own digital future, not be dictated to, says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 8— Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies, warning against a form of “technology colonialism” in which technologically advanced nations dictate how other countries develop and deploy their digital infrastructure. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development. Fahmi said Malaysia’s experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.

items.title: Police raid unlicensed KL entertainment outlet, detain 195 underage patrons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Police detained 195 underage teenagers and a premises manager in a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital after midnight last night. Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the teenagers detained in the operation, conducted at about 12.30 am, comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females. He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidate for Paya Rumput aims to ease voting process with personalised polling slips
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Paya Rumput state constituency Datuk Azman Abidin has introduced an initiative to help voters check their polling locations and channels ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14. Azman, popularly known as Tok Man, said he and his campaign team would assist voters in checking their polling details while campaigning, with the results printed on small slips and handed to them for reference. “Under this initiative, campaign workers only need to enter a voter’s identity card number to retrieve information on their polling location, including the school and assigned polling channel,” he told reporters after attending a courtesy visit and meet-and-greet programme with the Paya Rumput state constituency campaign machinery today.

items.title: Penang Sentral offers round-the-clock waiting space for travellers, says Zairil
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Nov 8 — Penang Sentral, an integrated transport hub and major commercial development, provides a 24-hour waiting area on Level 1 at its stage bus platform, equipped with basic facilities for passengers. Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the facility was intended for passengers waiting for buses or their next connecting transport service. He said Penang Sentral was operated by Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and not the state government, adding that the waiting area was not meant to serve as accommodation or an overnight stay facility.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of prolonged rain in four states until Wednesday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of continuous rain at the alert level for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu, until Wednesday. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan. In Pahang, the areas affected are Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while the warning covers the whole of Terengganu.

items.title: Melaka plans five-year push to transform Kota Laksamana into state capital
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 —Kota Laksamana has the potential to become the new state capital of Melaka due to rapid development that can catalyse economic growth and transform the state's landscape, says Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf said the development plan also encompasses areas under the Straits of Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone (SM-WEZ), covering commercial, residential, healthcare and tourism sectors. Commenting on preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, Ab Rauf said the state government has stepped up disaster preparedness, including identifying 102 flood hotspots across the state.

items.title: BN-Pakatan relationship unaffected by Najib pardon issue, says Zahid
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — Differences in political views and positions among parties in the Unity Government have not affected the smooth administration of the government, said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the working relationship between BN and Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the government remained good, with the administration of ministries and Cabinet meetings proceeding smoothly and professionally. Elaborating, the Deputy Prime Minister said differences in political approaches and positions among parties should be addressed maturely, particularly when political situations differ at the federal and state levels.

items.title: Flood-prone areas under close watch as wet weather looms in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 8 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department has stepped up patrols and monitoring in flash flood-prone areas throughout the state following forecasts of rain and thunderstorms until Tuesday. He said today’s forecast indicated rain in several areas in the morning, followed by thunderstorms in most areas in the afternoon and rain in most places at night. Mohamad Shoki said that on Tuesday, rain was forecast in several coastal areas in the morning, while conditions were expected to ease slightly in the afternoon and evening, although thunderstorms and rain were still forecast in some areas.

items.title: Was a BN convoy given priority? Two-car collision at Melaka traffic lights sparks questions
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — A Threads video is raising questions over whether traffic police gave a Barisan Nasional (BN) convoy priority at the time of a two-car accident at a junction on the Alor Gajah-Melaka Tengah-Jasin (AMJ) highway. On social media, someone remarked that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers and asked what had earned the group priority on the road. It noted that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers, and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.

items.title: Perak MMEA seizes vessel, probes unauthorised anchoring and reporting lapses
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 8 —The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Perak detained a cargo vessel suspected of violating the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952, about 4.3 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Jarak, near Lumut, yesterday. Its director, Maritime Captain Zainudin Mohd Zuki, said the Lumut Maritime Surveillance System radar detected the Gambian-registered vessel, prompting the Perak Maritime Headquarters Operations Centre to alert enforcement teams for inspection. He said the vessel had 21 crew members, including 11 Pakistanis, eight Iranians and two Indonesians.

items.title: AKPS detains 28-tonne buffalo meat shipment over import document irregularities
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) at Port Klang seized a consignment of buffalo meat, valued at RM413,728 and imported from India, at Port Klang on Friday (Nov 6). Port Klang AKPS commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said an inspection conducted by enforcement officers at 10.40am detected discrepancies between the halal certificate documents submitted and the information declared in the import permit. Following this, the entire consignment weighing 27,984 kilogrammes (kg) was seized for further investigation,” he said in a statement posted on the Port Klang AKPS Facebook page today.

items.title: Fake cops cheat retiree of RM179,490 in money laundering scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 —A 73-year-old retiree lost RM179,490 after falling victim to a Macau scam involving fraudsters posing as police officers and accusing him of money laundering and drug trafficking. Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the victim was initially contacted by two unidentified individuals claiming to be police officers, who instructed him to surrender his bank cards, cash and jewellery for investigation purposes. Hoo said the victim lodged a police report after realising he had been cheated.

items.title: Melaka lacks a real capital, says Ab Rauf, who wants Kota Laksamana to be it
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants to turn Kota Laksamana into Melaka’s state capital if it wins the seat in the coming state election, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. “God willing, I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the capital of Melaka,” he said at a campaign event at BN’s Kota Laksamana operations room here, attended by MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and BN candidate Melvin Chua Kew Wei. “So if we win Kota Laksamana, we will give the people of Kota Laksamana a centre that will become Melaka’s state capital,” he said.
